To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Stochastic resonance applied to microarray data reveals that genes considered silent by standard methods of analysis are in fact expressed in a periodic fashion, and that this expression is specific for the tissue of origin.”

the expression of genes below background noise can be detected using the method of stochastic resonance and that these genes have a periodic pattern consistent with expression of conventionally detected genes.
(1) Stochastic resonance reveals the expression of genes below the background noise of microarray signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the analysis of microarray data.
the analysis of the expression of genes in microarray experiments.
the detection of the expression of low-expressed or silent genes by the application of stochastic resonance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stochastic resonance method can be used to detect low expressed genes in microarrays.
the stochastic resonance method can be used for the detection of expression of low-expressed (and therefore conventionally undetected) genes.
the stochastic resonance is able to extract information from microarray data, which is hidden from traditional analysis, and to detect expression of low-expressed mammalian genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of the vast majority of mammalian genes is detectable at the level of microarray analysis, even if the signal is below the noise level.
the “Absent” genes are not really “Absent” but expressed at a very small level and can be detected by stochastic resonance analysis.
“Stochastic resonance reveals “pilot light” expression in mammalian genes”.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stochastic resonance can be used for the detection of genes below the background noise.
the genes that were considered “silent” by traditional analysis, are actually expressed.
the expression levels of many mammalian genes are lower than previously thought, but still detectable.
